records.public_claim_text: (See section V.A (5.1) above for guidance on what constitutes formality in quality risk management.) Higher levels of formality in quality risk management may require higher levels of structure in relation to risk-based decision-making.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: (See section V.A (5.1) above for guidance on what constitutes formality in quality risk management.) Higher levels of formality in quality risk management may require higher levels of structure in relation to risk-based decision-making.

records.public_claim_text: Managing and Minimizing Subjectivity (5.3) Subjectivity can impact every stage of a quality risk management process, especially the identification of hazards and the estimation of probability of occurrence and severity of harm.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Managing and Minimizing Subjectivity (5.3) Subjectivity can impact every stage of a quality risk management process, especially the identification of hazards and the estimation of probability of occurrence and severity of harm.

records.public_claim_text: While subjectivity cannot be completely eliminated from quality risk management activities, it may be controlled by addressing bias and assumptions, the proper use of quality risk management tools and maximizing the use of relevant data and sources of knowledge (see ICH Q10, section II.E.1 (1.6.1)).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: While subjectivity cannot be completely eliminated from quality risk management activities, it may be controlled by addressing bias and assumptions, the proper use of quality risk management tools and maximizing the use of relevant data and sources of knowledge (see ICH Q10, section II.E.1 (1.6.1)).

records.public_claim_text: Training of both industry and regulatory personnel in quality risk management processes provides for greater understanding of decision-making processes and builds confidence in quality risk management outcomes.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Training of both industry and regulatory personnel in quality risk management processes provides for greater understanding of decision-making processes and builds confidence in quality risk management outcomes.

records.public_claim_text: The Role of Quality Risk Management in Addressing Product Availability Risks Arising From Quality/Manufacturing Issues (6.1) Quality/manufacturing issues, including non-compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), are a significant cause of product availability issues (e.g., product shortages).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The Role of Quality Risk Management in Addressing Product Availability Risks Arising From Quality/Manufacturing Issues (6.1) Quality/manufacturing issues, including non-compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), are a significant cause of product availability issues (e.g., product shortages).

records.public_claim_text: When risk-based drug shortage prevention and mitigation activities are performed, the level of formality that is applied to those activities may vary (see section V.A (5.1)) and should be commensurate with the level of risk associated with a loss of availability of the product(s).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: When risk-based drug shortage prevention and mitigation activities are performed, the level of formality that is applied to those activities may vary (see section V.A (5.1)) and should be commensurate with the level of risk associated with a loss of availability of the product(s).

records.public_claim_text: A successful manufacturing partnership is strengthened by appropriate communication and collaboration mechanisms (See section II.G (2.7) of ICH Q10).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: A successful manufacturing partnership is strengthened by appropriate communication and collaboration mechanisms (See section II.G (2.7) of ICH Q10).

records.public_claim_text: Hazard Identification: The systematic use of information to identify potential sources of harm (hazards) referring to the risk question or problem description.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Hazard Identification: The systematic use of information to identify potential sources of harm (hazards) referring to the risk question or problem description.

records.public_claim_text: Quality System: The sum of all aspects of a system that implements quality policy and ensures that quality objectives are met.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Quality System: The sum of all aspects of a system that implements quality policy and ensures that quality objectives are met.

records.public_claim_text: Stakeholder: Any individual, group or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a risk.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Stakeholder: Any individual, group or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a risk.
